cards.note:
If you see gap and reflector in between outer lines you gonna be in ACT.

(South Australia might have gaps in outerlines but reflector in a gap is super rare there)
Guardrail ending, featuring a black dash on a yellow background, is almost exclusive to New South Wales and the ACT.
New South Wales is the only state to use red ‘No Stopping’ signs.
If you see more than couple yellow plates in Australia you should be in NSW
Rusty metal holey poles are unique to Northern Territory state in Australia.
This poletop is unique to QLD and most commonly you can find it on A6 highway.
These black markings are specific to electricity poles in Queensland(from Gold Coast to Sunshine Coast). They are often accompanied by diagonal numbers.

If you see this grayish long thin plate with numbers, sometimes with extra blue(or other color) little circle marking you gonna be in QLD(not in south east most likely because they use different marking).
If you see couple of those cool bottle trees planted next to the road you will be in Roma in Australia.

You can only find flat signposts in South Australia and Western Australia (in WA they mostly will be yellow but not always). You will also find rounded sign posts in SA (so don't rule SA if you see rounded one).
You can find these white property markers on the sides of roads in South Australia.
The iconic Stobie pole, made of steel and concrete, is specific to South Australia.(A few thousand of these poles can be found in other states, most notably Tasmania - super rare)

Metas for Tasmiania poles:

  • Olive-green possum guards
  • 90 degrees bend crossbar
  • this unique lamp arms
Victorian pole tops feature 3 circular coils; 2 on the sides, and 1 vertical one at the top.(sometimes might be missing the top one)
You can find these white hydrant poles that feature a blue circle and a red section on top of it in Victoria.(they have couple different designs but they all follow same color/shape +/- pattern)
Bollards with brown paint at the bottom are most commonly found in Western Australia.

Western Australia pole metas:

  • Trident pole top(can also be seen in Victoria)
  • Green painted bottom of poles
  • red/white sticker
  • yellow horizontal sticker
  • white and gray sticker
You can find these dark green property markers on the sides of roads in Western Australia.
Black-and-white stripy bollards are unique to Western Australia.
Yellow signposts are specific to Western Australia.
